opening_message:
Ticket 1: Erika Bolton (employee ID E002) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E002.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: E002 (Erika Bolton) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, admin requires the employee's role to own the system; Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist, not Analyst, so access is capped at write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: E002 (Erika Bolton) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin for Payroll exceeds max, so cap at read. Recommend granting read.
reason: E002 (Erika Bolton) requests admin access to Payroll, which is above any permitted maximum. However, the two agent notes conflict on employment type: HR reports full-time Analyst (max write, since Analyst does not own Payroll), while Security reports contractor with basic training (max read). Given this unresolved conflict, read is the only level permitted under both interpretations and cannot exceed policy. Admin was never permissible.
